Satellite passes over Bellevue, WA (47.61° N, 122.20° W)

Data generated 2026-10-17 12:53 PDT (window Sat 10-17 12:53 PDT to Tue 10-20 12:53 PDT). Predictions expire: the orbits are only valid near their measurement dates and errors grow each day. Pass times outside this window aren't covered. To refresh, run the hifi scripts again (see hifi/README.md: cd hifi; python3 scripts/build_elements.py; python3 scripts/gen_ephem.py; python3 scripts/post.py; python3 scripts/build_globe.py) and rebuild this page.

Shows passes that peak at least 20° above the horizon. All times are PDT (America/Los_Angeles). "Visible" means the satellite is in sunlight while the Bellevue sky is dark (Sun more than 6° below the horizon), so it can be seen by eye or with binoculars. Tier is the data quality, from A (best, error under 1 km) to E (very rough). "±t" is the 1-sigma timing uncertainty right now, and it grows over the window. Azimuth is in degrees clockwise from north.
